workflow: Reviewed and integrated individual worker commits from isolated worktrees into local Runner main. No pushes, pull requests, CI operations or MSI execution.

behavior.finalInstallerAuthentication: After acknowledged native UI exit, independently fetch the newest published release, asset metadata and source identity again. Require cached receipt and actual MSI bytes to match that fresh identity.
behavior.pathLifetime: Use the existing VerifiedFile guard to retain the MSI and complete ancestor path through Windows Installer process creation. Launcher then exits; no claim of full installer-lifetime or compromised-same-user isolation.
behavior.authorization: Missing handoffs fail. Consume a verified handoff before spawn so a failed spawn requires fresh confirmation and no removal error follows a successfully created installer.
behavior.releaseSelection: Choose numeric newest before asset validation, reject duplicate eligible versions and never fall back when the newest candidate is invalid.
behavior.metadata: Fresh ACL-protected Windows request directories; remove partial/error response bodies while retaining diagnostic logs. Atomically publish synced receipt/handoff bytes without overwriting existing files.
behavior.ui: Canonical Windows Installer version bounds and strictly newer versions required for available, downloaded and queued results.
behavior.powerShell: PowerShell 7.6+ baseline, typed ProcessStartInfo arguments, explicit native exit checks and UTF-8 stdout, bounded waits, non-reparse path ancestry, safe owned-stage cleanup, stronger MSI/release asset identities and native executable launcher selection.
behavior.brittlenessControls: No new dependencies or publisher/CDN certificate pins. Preserve supported HTTPS redirects. Hosted WiX builds and large uploads have explicit 600-second limits within workflow aggregate limits, without pinning a PowerShell patch release.
